newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: COSTA RICA SEEKS TO FREE UP DOMESTIC COFFEE PRICES.
newsitem.headline: COSTA RICA SEEKS TO FREE UP DOMESTIC COFFEE PRICES.

text.p: The Costa Rican coffee sector agreed Sunday to ask the government to free current controls on prices of coffee sold to domestic consumers, coffee representatives said.

The accord was reached at the XXVI National Coffee Congress organised by the Costa Rican Coffee Institute (ICAFE) on the grounds that current high international bean prices were driving domestic roasters into using and mix low grade beans to produce soluble coffee.

"Right now national roasters have to use the lowest possible quality coffee and mix it with the maximum allowed amount of sugar to cut costs," Guillermo Canet, the executive director of ICAFE told Reuters.
Canet said national coffee prices were fixed at 875 colons per kilo (around $3.75).
"The motion to ask the government to end controls on internal coffee prices was presented to the congress by the National Coffee Growers Chamber and was approved unanimously," Canet said.

It was also agreed to form a permanent commission to promote and continue to work on improving coffee quality in Costa Rica. The congress also decided to push to make ICAFE an independent and autonomous entity.
"It was decided to press the president and the congress to support a law that would give ICAFE independence," Canet added.

ICAFE is currently a semi-autonomous institution, financed with funds generated from coffee sales. Despite of being self-sufficient, it is subject to government budget controls and its funds are managed by the state, Canet said.
"This situation puts restraints on us and stops us spending more to do a better job, despite the fact that we have sufficient funds," Canet said.
